This reference maps generalized coordinates, joint orderings, kinematic
conventions, and bilateral grip decompositions across the shipped UpstreamDrift
golf multibody, biomechanics, and motion-capture modules at pinned commit
[`625a16e6`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/625a16e6897b88ab29fb5a64c65ecee820dd58f5).

::: {.callout-note title="Authority Boundary"}
**This establishes** `qpos` / velocity index order, joint type, axis, limit,
actuator name, and closed-loop equality constraints for four MuJoCo golf XML
definitions; the 35-DOF `golfer-scapula/2.0` Simscape articulated chain,
segment lengths, and signed log-column map; ISB anatomical angle Cardan
sequences, wrist per-side sign tables, and golf aliases; the pose-estimator
three-point included-angle convention ($\theta = \arccos(\hat{u}\cdot\hat{v})$);
and the $6\times 12$ two-hand grasp map and hand-split coordinates.

**This does not establish** full generated MJCF/URDF/OSIM tables for MyoSuite,
Drake, OpenSim, or Pinocchio, nor unvalidated Simscape wrist/leg/head DOFs.
Those extensions remain tracked under [AffineDrift #5621](https://github.com/D-sorganization/AffineDrift/issues/5621).
:::

## MuJoCo Motor-Driven Humanoids {#sec-mujoco-golf-maps}

Regenerate after changing the manifest pin:

```bash
python3 -m scripts.generate_golf_model_maps
```

## How to Read `q[i]` {#sec-reading-q}

Use the `qpos` index for configuration components and the `v` index for generalized
velocities. Motor actuators act on the listed hinge joints. `weld` and `connect`
equalities enforce grip closure and (in the advanced model) hip attachment without
adding independent coordinates; their forces depend on the MuJoCo solver.

## Simscape Articulated Model (`golfer-scapula/2.0`) {#sec-simscape-golfer-scapula}

The motion-capture reconstruction model (`golfer-scapula/2.0`,
`src/motion_capture/reconstruct/model/golfer.py`) places every body frame at
the Simscape `GolfSwing3D_Kinetic` sensor frame using identified constant pre/post
rotations:

$$\text{child} = \text{parent} \cdot R(\text{pre}) \cdot R_{\text{axes}}(q) \cdot R(\text{post})$$

where rotations are intrinsic with the first listed axis outermost, and relative
identifications solve $R_P^T R_C = A R(\pm q) B$ (maximum fit residual
$\le 2.7 \times 10^{-4}\text{ rad}$ across 620 logged frames; forward replay within
$\le 1.7 \times 10^{-3}\text{ rad}$ and $\le 0.6\text{ mm}$). Note that the
kinematic tree puts the `torso` revolute (`z`) **before** the `spine` universal
(`zx`) — the reverse of the prose order in the legacy MATLAB guide — and uses
asymmetric left/right arm axis labels (`left_scapula` `xz` / `left_shoulder` `xyz`
vs. `right_scapula` `yz` / `right_shoulder` `yzx`). The reconstruct world
($x$ target, $y$ up, $z$ golfer's right) maps to Simscape world ($z_s$ up,
$y_s$ golfer's right) via $(x_s, y_s, z_s) = (x, -z, y)$. Only the 23 trunk,
scapula, shoulder, elbow, and forearm DOFs (plus 3 root translations and 3 root
rotations in `SIMSCAPE_NAMES`) match logged sensors; wrist DOFs are named only and
leg/head DOFs are omitted from the MATLAB model.

```bash
python3 -m scripts.generate_golf_model_maps --simscape-only
```

{{< include _generated/golf-model-maps-simscape.qmd >}}

## ISB Anatomical Angle Conventions & Golf Aliases {#sec-isb-angle-conventions}

UpstreamDrift reports clinical/anatomical angles (`src/shared/python/biomechanics/joint_conventions.py`, `src/shared/python/anatomical_angles/`) using calibrated right-handed ISB frames (Wu et al. 2002/2005) and distinct golf-alias tables:

| Segment / Profile | Sequence | Ordered Components & Positive Sense | Singularity / Scope Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isb_thorax` & `trunk_pelvis` | `ZXY` | `extension` (`FE`), `right_lateral_flexion` (`LB`), `left_axial_rotation` (`AR`) | Decomposes `lab^T R_segment`; `forward_bend = -FE`; `FE, AR -> NaN` at `\|LB\| = 90°` |
| `isb_hip` | `ZXY` | `flexion_extension`, `adduction_abduction`, `internal_external_rotation` | Flexion-positive (opposite to spine extension-positive) |
| `isb_glenohumeral` / `isb_thoracohumeral` | `YXY` | `plane_of_elevation`, `negative_elevation`, `internal_rotation` | Middle angle negated (`negative_middle=True`); `0°` abduction vs `90°` flexion |
| `isb_elbow` | `ZXY` | `flexion`, `carrying_angle`, `pronation` | Source for forearm pronation (`forearm_in_humerus_rotation`) |
| `isb_wrist` | `ZXY` | `flexion`, `ulnar_deviation`, `axial_rotation` | Radius→3rd metacarpal (`OBSERVABILITY = fitted_grip_rotation`); `SIDE_SIGN`: `R=(1,1,1)`, `L=(1,-1,-1)`; 3rd angle is **not** forearm pronation; `\|ulnar\| = 90° -> NaN` |
| `grood_suntay_knee` | `XYZ` | `femoral_x_rotation`, `floating_axis_rotation`, `tibial_z_rotation` | Grood & Suntay (1983) floating-axis sequence |

In `src/shared/python/anatomical_angles/golf_aliases.py`, `WRIST_GOLF_ALIASES` maps
`"cupped"` to `-flexion`, `"bowed"` to `+flexion`, and `"hinge"` / `"cock"` to
`-ulnar_deviation`; `"release"` deliberately raises `ValueError` because it
names a dynamic swing event rather than a signed angle.

## Pose-Estimator Included Angles vs. Anatomical Flexion {#sec-pose-estimator-included-angle}

MediaPipe and OpenPose pipelines (`src/shared/python/pose_estimation/joint_angle_utils.py`,
`src/tools/video_analyzer/analyzer.py`) compute three-keypoint limb angles from
joint-to-proximal and joint-to-distal unit vectors:

$$\theta = \arccos(\hat{u} \cdot \hat{v}) \in [0, \pi] \quad (\text{or } [0^\circ, 180^\circ]).$$

Under this included-angle formula, a straight limb reads $\approx \pi\text{ rad}$
($180^\circ$), whereas ISB anatomical flexion (`anatomical_angles/limbs.py`) is
$0^\circ$ in neutral standing posture. For purely planar hinge motion,
$\text{flexion}_{\text{anat}} \approx 180^\circ - \theta$; in general 3D motion,
three-point angles mix planar flexion with ab/adduction and axial rotation and
cannot be equated directly with signed Cardan coordinates.

## Two-Hand Grasp Map and Hand-Split Coordinates {#sec-two-hand-grasp-map}

In `src/shared/python/loop_nullspace/grip_split.py`, bilateral six-axis hand
wrenches $y = (f_L, c_L, f_R, c_R) \in \mathbb{R}^{12}$ (each three force
components plus three free couple components at grip points $r_L, r_R$ about
their midpoint origin) map to the net club wrench $w = (F, M) \in \mathbb{R}^6$
via the $6 \times 12$ grasp map $G$:

$$w = G y = \begin{bmatrix} I_3 & 0 & I_3 & 0 \\ [\rho_L]_\times & I_3 & [\rho_R]_\times & I_3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} f_L \\ c_L \\ f_R \\ c_R \end{bmatrix}.$$

Every admissible hand-load allocation decomposes into equal-split plus internal
null-space coordinates $y = G^# w + K s$, where $G^#$ allocates half the net
wrench to each hand, $G K = 0$ ($K \in \mathbb{R}^{12\times 6}$), and
$s = \Phi y = \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}(f_R - f_L),\, \tfrac{1}{2}(c_R - c_L)\bigr)$
defines the six split coordinates $s_1$–$s_6$ (axial component positive when
pulling right relative to left along $d$, negative when squeezing; compare the
scalar point-force projection in `_ch05_two_hand_wrench.qmd`).
